html:
On 25 April 1974 young army officers overthrew the dictatorship in Portugal in an almost bloodless coup. Crowds put red carnations in the soldiers' rifles.

The officers' movement had grown tired of the colonial wars in Angola, Guinea-Bissau and Mozambique, which had lasted thirteen years and taken a large share of the budget. The signal to move was a banned song, Grândola, Vila Morena, played on the radio after midnight.

Within two years the colonies were independent, and hundreds of thousands of settlers came home as retornados. After a tense revolutionary period, a democratic constitution was adopted in 1976. Portugal joined the European Community in 1986. 25 April is Freedom Day. The revolution ended the regime of Salazar and inspired Spain's own transition.
sum: On 25 April 1974 young army officers overthrew the dictatorship in Portugal in an almost bloodless coup. Crowds put red carnations in the soldiers' rifles.
